name: Parmit Chilana
role: Associate Professor and Ebco-Eppich Research Chair
bio: Parmit Chilana is an Associate Professor and the Ebco-Eppich Research Chair in the School of Computing Science at Simon Fraser University (SFU), where she also serves as Associate Director of Research and Industry Relations. She is the co-founder and co-director of SFU’s Visual and Interactive Computing Institute (VINCI). Her research in human-computer interaction (HCI) investigates how people learn, create, and work with complex and emerging technologies, and develops novel interactive systems to make these technologies easier to understand and use. Her work spans software learnability, human-AI interaction, and interactive systems across domains including 3D modeling, education, health, and software development, with a particular focus on user diversity, learning, creativity, and human agency. Her research has received several honors, including the CS-CAN Outstanding Early Career Computer Science Researcher Award, an NSERC Discovery Accelerator Supplement, multiple Best Paper recognitions at venues such as ACM CHI, and the 2025 IEEE VL/HCC Most Influential Paper Award. Before joining SFU, she was an Assistant Professor at the University of Waterloo. She received her PhD from the University of Washington, where she co-founded AnswerDash, a venture-funded startup that commercialized her dissertation research on crowdsourced contextual help.

name: Eva Mackamul
bio: Dr Eva Mackamul is a Postdoctoral Fellow working with Dr Parmit Chilana in the Interactive Experiences Lab at SFU. In particular, she is interested in user perception and interpretation of interfaces and their affordances and how they translate to discoverability and learnability. Previously, she worked as a Postdoctoal Fellow at the Université Grenoble Alpes on the perception of fragility in Shape-Changing Interfaces and completed her PhD focused on improving the discovery of touch-based interactions through visual signifiers at Inria de l’Université de Lille.

name: Afra Liu
bio: Afra is a PhD student co-supervised by Dr. Parmit Chilana and Dr. Nick Vincent. Her research interests broadly focus on human–AI interaction and AI literacy.

name: David Wong
bio: David Wong is pursuing his PhD in Computing Science at Simon Fraser University, under the supervision of Prof. Parmit Chilana and Diana Cukierman. Before that, he was the founder and chief of Learning Technologies Office at Universidad Privada del Norte, in Peru, for eight years. In that position, David developed several tools to help teachers and students to achieve their educational goals using technology. David's main areas of interest are in Human-Computer Interaction, Internet of Things (IoT), and Computing Education. He holds a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science from National University of Trujillo, Peru.

name: Aham Gupta
bio: Aham is a Master's student supervised by Dr. Parmit Chilana. His research focuses on designing and evaluating instructor-centered AI tools that integrate into teaching workflows, thereby supporting instructors in their teaching tasks.

name: Kanak Gautam
bio: Kanak is a Master's student in Computer Science at Simon Fraser University, working with Dr. Parmit Chilana. Her research focuses on HCI and user experiences in AI-assisted creative tools, especially generative 3D modeling systems.

name: Huy Bui
bio: Huy is a Master's student in Computing Science at Simon Fraser University, supervised by Dr. Parmit Chilana. His research interests are broadly software learnability and human-AI interaction. Before starting his MSc, he worked as a software developer, building and maintaining applications and data infrastructure.

name: Alex Noh
bio:
I am an undergraduate researcher at Simon Fraser University with broad interest in eXtended Reality (XR), Human-AI Interactions, and Accessibility, particularly building, evaluating, and studying XR & AI systems that enable novel interactions and augments human abilities and cognition. My current research explores how we can use these emerging technologies to better support people with ADHD.

Additionally, I have had various non-research experience, including teaching, working with children/students with disabilities, SWE practicum at Amazon Web Services and technical internship at a local animation studio.

name: Poorvi Bhatia
bio: I’m a fourth-year Computing Science undergraduate at Simon Fraser University interested in the intersection of Human-Computer Interaction and Artificial Intelligence. As an undergraduate research assistant at the ixLab, I had the opportunity to contribute to research on how people learn and interact with generative AI tools and how AI literacy develops in creative communities. These experiences have strengthened my interest in HCI research and human-centered AI.

name: Isabelle Kwan
bio: Isabelle is a computing science student at SFU who completed an NSERC USRA with Dr. Parmit Chilana in 2024. During her time in the lab, she contributed to two projects: “Milestones: the design and field evaluation of a semi-automated tool for promoting self-directed learning among online learners” and “How Creatives Approach GenAI Image Generation: Tensions Between Structured Guidance, Self-Experimentation, and Creative Autonomy.” As well, she helped manage, run studies, and assist with many additional projects that involved haptics, explainable AI, and accessibility tools. Currently, she continues her HCI research through several other labs, both at SFU and at the University of Waterloo, and hopes to continue her research into graduate studies! Though she no longer works full-time in the lab, she still loves to attend meetings every once in a while and spend time with the amazing ixLab members.

name: Anjali Khurana
bio: Anjali Khurana completed her PhD in 2026, focusing on designing and developing LLM-based assistants and copilots for software help-seeking and AR/mixed reality applications that foster effective human–AI collaboration and help users form accurate mental models of these emerging technologies. During her Ph.D., she interned with Microsoft Research's FATE Group in New York, where she explored transparency and user control in LLMs, broadening her interests to include interpretability and explainable AI. She is currently a Research Scientist at Hitachi in Montreal.

name: Rimika Chaudhury
bio: Rimika Chaudhury completed her PhD in 2025. Her research focused on designing visual and interactive self-monitoring tools to support informal and self-directed learning, including systems that help learners track and reflect on their progress. She is currently a Postdoctoral Fellow at McGill University.

name: Narges Ashtari
bio: Narges Ashtari completed her PhD in 2024. Her research focused on understanding and lowering barriers to creating AR/VR applications, particularly for novice developers using emerging authoring tools. During her PhD, she interned at Meta and Google. She is currently a UX Researcher at Meta in the USA.

name: Amir Jahanlou
bio: Amir Jahanlou completed his PhD in 2023. His research focused on lowering barriers to creating motion graphics, including example-based approaches that help novice designers learn and build animations by reusing and adapting existing examples. He is currently a Staff Product Manager at LottieFiles.

name: Laton Vermette
bio: Laton Vermette completed his PhD in 2022. His research focused on designing interactive systems to help people learn and customize complex software, including example-based approaches for discovering new features. During his PhD, he interned at Microsoft. He is currently a Software Engineer and UX Researcher at the Internet Archive.
